subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw memory status treat live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth, or should memory plugins expose a passive local status contract for CLI status/doctor?
rationale: The current code can avoid the old false `unavailable` row, but the complete fix depends on the intended status semantics and plugin boundary rather than a purely mechanical one-line repair.

options.title: Use live gateway truth
options.body: Have memory-reporting status call the running gateway for runtime/provider health and avoid local plugin startup when the gateway is reachable.

options.title: Add passive plugin status
options.body: Define a narrow plugin status hook that cannot perform heavyweight startup and use it for CLI-local memory details.

options.title: Accept not checked
options.body: Treat the current `not checked` mitigation as sufficient for this issue and leave broader local-plugin side effects to the related open issue.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway truth
recommendation.body: Have memory-reporting status call the running gateway for runtime/provider health and avoid local plugin startup when the gateway is reachable.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal for both the memory runtime routing and the custom memory status repair points to this owner.
